newsitem.title: USA: Petrie Retail refinances, sells unit's receivables.
newsitem.headline: Petrie Retail refinances, sells unit's receivables.

text.p: Petrie Retail Inc said Monday that it has completed its debtor-in-possession refinancing and sold its Winkelman's unit's credit receivables.
In the refinancing, Chase Manhattan Bank, a unit of Chase Manhattan Corp, has signed a commitment letter to provide it a $96 million credit facility, it said.
The privately held women's apparel retailer said the commitment letter extends its debtor-in-possession financing for two years to April 1999.
The financing is backed by a $50- million letter of credit provided by an affaliate of E.M. Warburg, Pincus LLC, it said.

Petrie, which has been operating under Chjapter 11 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code since October 1995, also said it had repaid $45 million of its secured debt and sold the charge card receivables of its Winkelman's store chain to Shoppers Charge Accounts Co, a division of Hudson United Bank of Mahwah, N.J.
Under an agreement, Shoppers wil operate Winkelman's credit business, which accounts for $40 million in sales a year, for five years, it said.
The company said it has also closed an additional 104 stores in its Petrie Core stores.

It said it will now focus on its remaining 306 core stores and 407 G+G/Rave stores and 61 Winkelman's stores. The closings involve core stores under the name Petrie, Maryann's, Stuarts, Jean Nicole and Resource. It said no Winkelman's or G+G/Rave stores will be affected.

"The new bank financing we have received , together with proceeds from the sale of Winkelman's charge card receivables, provide us the ability to pay off our prepetition secured debt and the financial resources we need to operate our stores and place us in a position to emerge from Chaptedr 11," said Edwin Holman, chairman and chief executive officer of the company.
